rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct-match exists. PGS000753 is preferred because it is disease-focused (AAA-specific MVP paper), has explicit PRS effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and avoids reliance on full-model AUROC-only reporting. The main limitation is that it is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2, while several newer genome-wide shrinkage scores exist but mostly report only full-model discrimination (or weak PRS-comparable metrics) and/or come from framework/portability studies, making cross-model performance comparison uncertain. Runners-up are ranked by remaining support: PGS003973/PGS003972 are disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis PRS-CS scores but report only full-model C-index/AUROC with unknown covariates; PGS002054 and PGS001784 provide PRS-comparable partial-r / covariates-regressed-out R2 but are from portability/framework-style papers, which is discounted when disease-focused alternatives exist. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target trait alcohol dependence via trait_efo (either "alcohol dependence" or "alcohol dependence measurement") and phenotyping_reported (AUD/AUD criteria). PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder" and provides a clear, PRS-comparable effect metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900), with development cohorts listed as MVP and UKB. Main limitation: no PRS-only AUC/R2 is reported (only an OR contrast), covariates are unknown, and evaluation is EUR-only despite multi-ancestry GWAS composition.

Runners-up: PGS000201 and PGS000202 are close phenotype matches (DSM-5 AUD criteria count, log-transformed) but are labeled as "Problematic alcohol use" with trait_efo="alcohol dependence measurement" rather than the disease EFO; they also only report small incremental ΔR² (0.01192 and 0.00456) and beta estimates, with UKB-only development and no PRS-only AUC/R². Between them, PGS000201 is stronger than PGS000202 due to higher ΔR² and larger validation n (7,599 vs 1,251). PGS002739 is a direct AUD/alcohol dependence EFO match but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean (AFR 100%) and uses a gene-based PRS-CSx model with very low variant count (858); it reports OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76 (1.32–2.34), but its ancestry-specific evaluation makes it less generally supported absent a specified target ancestry. Overall, evidence is sufficient to pick a preferred direct-match model but remains limited by missing PRS-only discrimination metrics and incomplete covariate comparability, so the direct-match quality is sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping labels. PGS004913 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused for alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, reports PRS-comparable variance explained (R²=0.029) and an OR top vs bottom deciles of 4.4, and uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), making its reported signal more interpretable as PRS contribution than models reporting only full-model discrimination. Main limitation: its training/validation sample sizes are modest (training n=3,037; validation n=3,360) and the reported R² is not explicitly stated as PRS-only vs full-model, so comparability remains imperfect.

Runners-up: PGS001777 is also disease-focused and reports a strong stratification OR (top 20% vs bottom 20% OR=6.18) but is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and has small validation (n=1,390) with only full-model AUROC=0.671. PGS000704 has very large development/validation in UKB and a modern multi-PRS snpnet approach with many variants, but its only reported discrimination is a full-model C-index/AUC=0.711 (not PGS-only) and it comes from a broad biomarker genetics paper rather than a cirrhosis-focused study, so the apparent performance advantage is discounted per the provided domain guidance.

All 19 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping spans Angina/I20/PheCode 411.3). Best-supported pick: PGS001262 because it has strong endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed angina), reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.58683) and PGS-only R² (0.01304) that are plausible relative to the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.009–0.014), and uses only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). Main limitation: it comes from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust; also its very high full-model AUROC (0.807) is likely covariate-driven (incremental AUROC only 0.0098), so it should not be over-interpreted as PRS strength.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001261 is very similar framework/sparse design but targets angina pectoris time-to-event; it has slightly lower PGS-only AUROC (0.58233) and R² (0.01228) than PGS001262 and a less preferred TTE endpoint for generic disease status. (2) PGS001260 is the non-TTE angina sibling with slightly weaker PGS-only metrics (AUROC 0.58108; R² 0.01185). (3) PGS004527 (I20 angina) has a moderate-to-strong per-SD OR (1.429) and a direct ICD10 endpoint, but lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R² and has unknown covariates, lowering comparability. (4) PGS005048 (PheCode 411.3) reports a strong OR (1.487) and a high full-model C-index (0.7669), but the C-index appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), training sample is listed as N/A, and the paper is a methods-comparison context, so evidence is less directly comparable than the PGS-only-metric framework siblings. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to ankylosing spondylitis), so a direct-match exists. Among the pool, PGS002089 is best supported because it is a non-sparse, genome-wide-style score (LDpred2; 22,026 variants) from the UKB portability study and it reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0919 with CI) in European validation, providing more directly comparable PRS signal than candidates that report only full-model AUROC or lack PRS-only metrics. Key limitation: the strongest-looking AUROCs (e.g., ~0.79 in the Taiwanese EAS study) are full-model AUROCs with unknown covariates and are not stated as PGS-only, making them non-comparable; meanwhile the UKB framework/portability context is itself a known weakness for external generalization per the provided domain guidance. This leaves meaningful uncertainty and competition between the UKB-derived scores (PGS002089/PGS001267/PGS001268/PGS001876) and the EAS-only disease-focused scores, hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL and moderate confidence. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely aligned aortic-valve-function measurement scores that still use incident aortic stenosis phenotyping (PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with large variant count (~1.12M), and it reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), so it is not directly interpretable as PRS-only performance; no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, lowering certainty. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis score with a moderate-strong HR (1.64) and large variant count but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS005255 and PGS005256 are aortic stenosis–adjacent measurement-labeled scores yet still use incident aortic stenosis phenotyping and show HR 1.53; the remaining candidates are hypertrophic cardiomyopathy scores (not direct matches), with PGS004911 placed next only because it has stronger reported metrics than the other HCM entries, despite being phenotype-mismatched to aortic stenosis.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including two models explicitly labeled with EFO=arthritis (PGS001135: “Arthritis (nos)”; PGS004477/PGS004547: “M13 (Other arthritis)”). PGS001135 is the best-supported direct match because it has the cleanest phenotype alignment to generic arthritis (phenotyping_reported: “Arthritis (nos)”) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC, enabling interpretation beyond a covariate-driven full-model AUROC. The main limitation is that PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores; additionally, its PRS-only signal is modest. Runners-up are other direct EFO=arthritis models: PGS004547 and PGS004477 (both “M13 (Other arthritis)”) but they report only an OR without PRS-only AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, reducing comparability. Because the remaining visible list contains many arthritis subtypes (RA, OA, gout, etc.) rather than generic arthritis, the next best-supported near-direct umbrella arthritis proxy is osteoarthritis (PGS001290, PGS001882), but these are not exact arthritis endpoints, so they are ranked below the EFO=arthritis models. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for asthma are present (multiple models with trait_efo=asthma and asthma diagnosis/incident endpoints). The best-supported direct-match choice from the visible evidence is PGS002061 because it is an asthma PRS with a direct asthma endpoint, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with large variant count (793,375), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.1184, CI 0.1045–0.1322) in a large UKB-derived evaluation context; among the two UKB portability-family asthma scores shown, it has slightly stronger reported PRS-comparable performance than its sibling PGS001849 (partial-r 0.1135). Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support combining endpoint fidelity and availability of PRS-comparable metrics/effect sizes while discounting framework-style or covariate-heavy packaging: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; asthma; reports AUROC 0.659 and Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out 0.048844), PGS001787 (same study family; AUROC 0.64; R2 0.035168; very large evaluation sample), and then the snpnet UKB framework asthma models (PGS001344 and PGS001341) which have explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 but are penalized as pan-trait framework-derived despite decent metrics. Main limitation: several strong-looking alternatives exist with different study archetypes and non-uniform metric comparability (many report only full-model AUROC or effect sizes, some have unknown/heavy covariates, and endpoints vary: incident, pediatric, doctor-diagnosed, algorithmic), so the evidence does not uniquely identify a single clearly superior asthma PRS across contexts. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo includes atopic eczema). Ranking is driven primarily by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) and then by PRS-comparable performance evidence and structural/method signals.

PGS002755 is best supported because it targets incident atopic dermatitis (clean, generic disease endpoint aligned to the target trait) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), with a reported HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (EUR eval; n=337,910). Its main limitation is that it reports no PRS-only AUROC/R², and the HR is modest.

Runners-up: PGS004587 also uses an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint with an HR=1.153 (n=337,910) but is structurally weaker (23 GWAS-significant SNPs) and has a smaller effect size than PGS002755. PGS001773 is disease-focused on moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (aligned but subtype-restricted) and reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with covariates, which domain guidance says should not be treated as PRS-only evidence; additionally the very high full-model metrics are not sanity-checkable against the provided heritability ceiling without PRS-only metrics. PGS003486 and PGS003459 are further penalized because their phenotyping is paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients (therapy/context-specific endpoint mismatch for generic atopic eczema risk), despite reporting modest full-model AUROCs (~0.57–0.59) and ORs.

Direct-match candidates are abundant (all listed models map to atrial fibrillation / atrial fibrillation and flutter). PGS005168 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation), disease-focused multi-cohort development (large AF meta-analysis with many contributing cohorts), and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) with only basic/standard covariates plus CHARGE-AF adjustment (noted in domain guidance as a negative packaging signal, but here it is used as a covariate rather than a horizon-specific risk-wrapper). Key limitation: the reported metric is a full-model C-index (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence below High.

Runners-up: PGS005313 is also disease-focused and reports strong AUROC (0.78 with tight CI) and OR (1.82) but is evaluated in MAE-only, reducing generalizability vs EUR-evaluated candidates. PGS002814 has very large GWAS training (n=1,150,799) and strong OR (~1.94) with AUROC 0.74, but is developed/validated in East Asian context (EAS eval), making it less directly comparable for generic use. PGS000016 (LDpred, genome-wide) has explicit PRS-only R2 (0.029) and basic covariates, but is older and shows lower PRS-only variance explained relative to newer disease-focused meta-analysis options. PGS000331 is disease-focused multi-cohort with incident AF endpoint and HR 1.62 / C-index 0.751, but has smaller training (n=21,813) and less compelling performance evidence than the top selections. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct-match in the sense that their trait_efo includes atrial flutter; however, only PGS001263 is specifically phenotyped/reported as “Atrial flutter” (not a combined AF+flutter endpoint), giving it the strongest endpoint fidelity for the target. It also provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.61716; PGS-only R2=0.02517) and basic covariates, and its PGS-only R2 is below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so nothing is obviously inconsistent. Main limitation: PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; meanwhile the portability-paper models (PGS001841/PGS002050) use genome-wide shrinkage/penalized regression and larger training n but lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, making them hard to compare on PRS-comparable performance. Runners-up: PGS001339 is closest by metrics but has a time-to-event combined AF+flutter endpoint (weaker specificity). Between the two portability models, PGS002050 (LDpred2, genome-wide) is structurally preferred over PGS001841 (penalized regression) with essentially identical endpoint/covariates and very similar partial-r, but both remain limited by missing PRS-only AUROC/R2.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder). PGS000327 is best supported because its endpoint fidelity is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder”), it comes from an ASD-focused publication (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”), and it reports supportive PRS-relevant evidence including an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) and an R² metric (full_model_r2=0.0245) in European validation. PGS002790 is a weaker direct match despite the same trait_reported/trait_efo because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly different (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”), suggesting endpoint mismatch/metadata incoherence; its reported partial R² is smaller (0.00546) and it lacks effect-size evidence. Overall confidence is limited because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUROC/R²), and the selected R² values appear to be full-model/partial metrics rather than unambiguously PRS-only.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS000452 because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest reported discrimination/effect evidence among the comparable MGI-evaluated siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (European validation) with a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (and top-1% vs rest OR 3.61). Close runners-up are PGS000454 (very similar endpoint/covariates with essentially identical AUROC 0.632 and OR 1.661), then PGS000456 (AUROC 0.630, OR 1.633) and PGS000458 (AUROC 0.628, OR 1.634), all sharing the same disease endpoint and covariate structure, making them highly comparable. PGS000730 is next-best among the remaining set due to direct endpoint labeling and a strong per-SD OR 1.57 with large evaluation n=88,924, but it is penalized by unknown covariates and less directly comparable performance reporting (AUROC reported without CI and no PRS-only metrics). Confidence is Moderate rather than High because several near-clone MGI models (PGS000452/454/456/458) have extremely similar endpoint/covariates and very small metric differences, and none report PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting decisive separation. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo including “bilirubin metabolism disease”. The strongest endpoint fidelity is for PGS001824 and PGS002032 because both have trait_reported and phenotyping_reported exactly “Disorders of bilirubin excretion” (a direct instantiation of bilirubin metabolism disease), whereas PGS000924 uses a broader combined endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) and is explicitly time-to-event, which domain guidance flags as a potential endpoint-fidelity weakness when the target is a generic disease concept. Between the two exact-endpoint siblings (PGS001824 vs PGS002032), the visible performance evidence is effectively identical (same partial correlation 0.0716 with overlapping CIs; no PRS-only AUROC/R² reported), so method/structure becomes the main differentiator: LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 19,768 variants (PGS002032) is structurally favored over penalized regression with 22 variants (PGS001824). However, because both come from the same UKB portability framework paper and lack PRS-comparable AUC/R², and because the only available metric is partial-r (not directly comparable to AUROC/R²), the evidence does not support a clearly high-quality winner; thus DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL. PGS001824 is selected narrowly due to exact endpoint match plus simpler, more interpretable small-variant construction given the absence of any reported PRS-only AUROC/R² to confirm that the much larger LDpred2 model actually improves discrimination in this setting; this tie-break is weak and keeps confidence moderate. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (PGS002786 bipolar disorder; PGS002787 bipolar I; PGS002788 bipolar II), so this is a direct-match selection. However, all three models come from the same publication family, use the same method (SDPR), have similar very large variant counts, are EUR-only for GWAS/EVAL, and—critically—have phenotyping_reported fields that appear misaligned with the target disease endpoint (reported as cognitive/behavioral measures rather than bipolar diagnosis). Performance evidence is limited to small partial R² values (all ~0.0025–0.0031) with no PRS-only AUC/R², and covariates are basic (age, PCs1-3) across all, leaving little to differentiate quality. PGS002786 is chosen as the best-supported direct match primarily because its trait_reported/trait_efo most directly matches the target (‘Bipolar disorder’), but confidence is low due to endpoint-fidelity ambiguity and near-indistinguishability among the sibling models; runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support (bipolar I and bipolar II are still direct but narrower subtype matches).

All three visible candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target umbrella concept (blood coagulation disease), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS002034 is preferred because it targets a clearly coagulation-disease diagnosis phenotype ("Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors") and, among the two otherwise near-clone congenital-deficiency models from the same publication/UKB framework, it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45) while showing essentially identical partial-r performance (0.0563 vs 0.0562), making it the structurally stronger sibling given no other differentiating metrics. PGS001826 is the closest runner-up as the near-identical sibling with comparable endpoint and nearly identical partial-r but weaker structural properties (much smaller variant set). PGS001033 is ranked below both because its endpoint is time-to-event ("TTE other coagulation defects"), it is an extremely sparse 1-variant snpnet model, and it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as a systematic generalization weakness; although it reports AUROC, the evidence is still less reliable than the more endpoint-specific congenital-deficiency models. Overall confidence is low because none of the candidates provides strong, directly comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics (the congenital-deficiency models lack AUROC/R2 entirely and only report partial-r), and the available models represent narrow sub-phenotypes rather than a single clear, broad "blood coagulation disease" endpoint.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for the target trait (breast carcinoma / breast cancer). The strongest-supported option in the visible list is PGS004153 because it is a direct breast cancer endpoint (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), uses a multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; domain knowledge: multi-score aggregation is a strong structural positive), and reports strong standalone discrimination among the visible candidates (full_model_auc=0.6625 with covariates explicitly 0, plus strong effect sizes OR=1.83 and beta=0.602) in a sizable evaluation (n=48,968; EUR/SAS mix). Runners-up are selected from the same coherent high-performing cluster in the same publication family (Am J Hum Genet 2023-12-19, same endpoint and covariates=0), prioritizing those with the next-best reported AUROC/R2 and similarly strong OR/beta: PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV; AUROC~0.6598; R2~0.0739; OR~1.81), PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto; AUROC~0.6598; R2~0.0736; OR~1.81), PGS004083 (PRS-CS-auto; AUROC~0.6553; R2~0.0697; OR~1.77), and PGS004069 (megaprs.CV; AUROC~0.6558; R2~0.0709; OR~1.78). Main limitation: comparability across the broader candidate pool is constrained because many other direct-match models report only full-model metrics with nonzero/unknown covariates or different endpoint framing (incident vs prevalent, personal history, risk-model packaging), so while this internally consistent cluster is best-supported by the visible evidence, confidence is not maximal.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=celiac disease; phenotyping_reported consistently references coeliac/celiac disease, with some restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers or combined with gluten sensitivity). PGS000316 is best supported because it has an explicitly aligned endpoint (“Coeliac disease”), is from a disease-focused clinical-care/diagnosis-oriented study (not a pan-trait or portability framework), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with CI) with very large validation (n=379,767), making it the most evidence-rich disease-focused option in this list. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown, so PRS-only performance comparability is unclear; this keeps confidence below High.

Runners-up: PGS001301 has explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.8287; PGS R2=0.1422; full-model AUROC=0.8335) but is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable than disease-focused models when such models exist. PGS000040 is disease-focused and reports very high full-model AUROC=0.90, but lacks PRS-only metrics and has unknown covariates, making the AUC hard to interpret. PGS000042 and PGS000041 are disease-focused but restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint narrower than generic celiac disease) and have only full-model AUROC (~0.73), so they rank below the broader-endpoint disease-focused options. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported overall because it comes from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis explicitly aimed at risk stratification, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (2,894,555), and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with basic covariates (age, smoking), consistent with a disease-focused design. However, confidence is limited because it reports only full-model discrimination (C-index 0.613) without PRS-only metrics, and several other direct-match models have similarly limited/comparably non-PRS-only performance reporting.

Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 are coherent incident cervical cancer models with large European validation (n=211,795) and similar HR (~1.21–1.22) and C-index (~0.75), but they are GWAS-hits style (10 variants) and their reported AUROC/C-index are full-model with multiple epidemiologic covariates, making PRS-only strength hard to compare. PGS005165 is an East Asian-specific GWAS-hits model (15 variants) with HR=1.2 and EAS evaluation, supportive as a direct match but less broadly transportable from the visible evidence. PGS001299 (snpnet, 24 variants) provides explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.55; PGS R2 ~0.0026) but is from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which domain guidance flags as less reliable than disease-focused models when direct disease-focused options exist.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis by trait fields, but the evidence is mixed and often lacks PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²), lowering certainty. PGS002072 is preferred because it targets a closely aligned endpoint (“Cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”), comes from the same UKB portability study as a near-clone alternative, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (428,587), and has the strongest available comparable metric among the portability siblings (partial-r 0.098 vs 0.0948 for PGS001861) with similar covariates and validation context. Main limitation: the top candidate is from a portability/framework-style UKB study and reports only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), so direct evidence of standalone PRS discrimination is limited.

Runners-up: PGS001861 is the closest sibling (same endpoint/covariates/publication) but slightly weaker partial-r and smaller variant count. PGS004546 and PGS004476 are exact ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis endpoints and report moderate per-SD ORs (1.30 and 1.22 respectively), but have unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable discrimination metrics, making them harder to rank above the portability pair. PGS001174 is an exact cholelithiasis time-to-event endpoint with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC, but it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“813 traits”) which domain guidance flags as prone to poorer external generalization; its PGS-only R² (0.028) is below the local h2 ceiling (h2_obs 0.0214; liability 0.1372) and thus plausible, but the framework penalty and TTE endpoint keep it behind the more endpoint-faithful, genome-wide shrinkage portability scores. PGS005150 is EAS-only evaluation and reports only a beta effect size without comparable discrimination metrics, so it is less broadly supported in this context. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All listed candidates are direct matches to chronic kidney disease via trait_efo and generally CKD-relevant phenotyping. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD stage 3+ (eGFR <45) with a disease-focused publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”, Nat Med), large development sample (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and strong effect-size evidence (OR=1.47) alongside a reported AUROC (0.78, but noted as full-model). Key limitation: its reported AUROC is full-model with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so PRS-only discrimination cannot be directly compared across models.

Runners-up: PGS005090 has very strong reported metrics (AUROC=0.9, R²=0.1) and CKD stage 3+ focus in African-ancestry evaluation, but comparability across ancestries and lack of PRS-only metrics keep it behind the broadly evaluated Nat Med CKD score. PGS005113 shows a solid OR=1.35 with CKDGen training and relatively clean demographic/PC covariates, but lacks comparable discrimination metrics. PGS004889 targets incident CKD (without diabetes) with multi-ancestry evaluation and HR=1.3, but the endpoint is restricted (incident, non-diabetic) and includes a bundled clinical risk score covariate, reducing PRS comparability. PGS002757 is a straightforward CKD PRS-CS score with OR=1.15 but weaker effect size evidence than the above.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (with one emphysema subtype). The strongest overall evidence package among the COPD-labeled models is PGS001783: it is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus an AUROC value (0.74) albeit not explicitly PGS-only. This R2 is also consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0388), supporting metric plausibility.

Main limitation: several candidates come from framework-style publications (including PGS001783/PGS001788 from the Global Biobank analyses paper and PGS001332/133/134 from the UKB 813-traits sparse framework), and multiple models have incomplete or non-comparable performance reporting (e.g., only full-model AUROC, partial-r, or only OR). Main limitation: the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), so discrimination comparability across candidates remains imperfect; several alternatives also have large EUR validations and similar endpoints, lowering certainty.

Runner-up ordering: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer) and show similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) with standard covariates; PGS000076 is the original 19-variant GWS model and PGS000787 is a closely related re-weighting, so both remain strong but do not exceed PGS004908’s OR/AUROC evidence. PGS004690 is a genome-wide shrinkage-style model (AnnoPred; 6.35M variants) with kidney cancer endpoint but has only a modest AUROC (0.5644) and unknown covariates, making its evidence weaker than the top cluster. PGS000722 is endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer) with moderate AUROC (0.567) but minimal covariate detail (genotyping array only) and no effect sizes, placing it behind the above.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS000708 (trait_reported/trait_efo: Kidney failure; phenotyping_reported: diabetic kidney failure), PGS004492 (N18 chronic renal failure; trait_efo: kidney failure), and PGS004562 (N18 chronic renal failure; trait_efo: kidney failure). PGS000708 is preferred because it has the strongest visible endpoint fidelity to kidney failure as a disease outcome (explicit kidney failure phenotype rather than an ICD-code label alone) and provides the most informative performance evidence in-context (C-index/full_model 0.779 plus HR 1.19 with CI), whereas PGS004492/PGS004562 report only an OR without AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, limiting comparability. However, the choice remains sub-optimal because PGS000708’s phenotyping is restricted to diabetic kidney failure (a subtype constraint relative to generic kidney failure), and its reported discrimination is full-model (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004562 and PGS004492 are exact kidney-failure EFO matches (N18 chronic renal failure) but lack comparable performance metrics and covariate transparency; PGS002237 and PGS004158 are not kidney-failure EFO matches (CKD stage 3+ / CKD or dialysis) but are closely related endpoints with stronger reported discrimination/effect sizes and clearer disease-focused validation context than other CKD candidates. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target (knee osteoarthritis / gonarthrosis of knee) via trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002767 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: knee osteoarthritis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants), and reports a comparatively strong PRS effect size (OR=1.35 per SD, 95% CI 1.3–1.4) in EUR evaluation (n=39,444), which is the most PRS-comparable performance evidence available among the genome-wide scores here. However, confidence is limited because several other direct-match models have incomplete or non-PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., only full-model AUROC or only OR/HR without clear PRS-only AUC/R²), and one candidate (PGS001192) provides PRS-only metrics but comes from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (a negative study-archetype signal), making the overall ranking evidence somewhat heterogeneous rather than decisively convergent. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 5 visible candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = late-onset Alzheimer's disease). The strongest direct-match evidence comes from the coherent Neurology study family (PGS000053/PGS000054): both target familial late-onset AD, use the same 21 genome-wide significant variants, adjust for basic covariates (age, sex), and report per-SD odds ratios (a PRS-comparable signal when AUC/R2 are missing). Between these siblings, PGS000054 is preferred because it shows a stronger reported effect size (OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.21–1.37), and the domain guidance treats OR≥1.5 per SD as strong discriminative evidence. Main limitation: none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2; several have unknown covariates or non-disease endpoints (notably PGS002289’s phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction rather than AD diagnosis), so overall support is incomplete and the choice remains moderately uncertain.

Runner-up ordering: PGS000053 remains the closest sibling with clean covariates and direct disease endpoint but weaker OR; PGS000334 has a direct LO-AD endpoint and reports an R²=0.191 but it is a C+T score with unknown covariates and the domain guidance flags very high R² for thresholding methods as potentially non-comparable/suspect; PGS004918 has a direct endpoint but is pathway-restricted (8 SNPs) with small dev/validation (n=136) and only full-model AUROC reported (0.731) which is not a PRS-only metric; PGS002289 is least aligned on endpoint fidelity because its reported phenotype is cognitive performance interaction rather than AD case-control status despite the LO-AD label.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (lung cancer) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, with some being broader composites (e.g., lung and bronchus cancer) or restricted subgroups (e.g., early-onset, never-smokers). PGS004860 is best supported in the visible metadata because it has a directly aligned endpoint (incident lung cancer), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2; ~1.14M variants), and reports strong discrimination in its selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.893 with tight CI) plus an effect size (OR 1.33). However, confidence is not High because the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), and covariates include smoking status and other factors that can inflate full-model discrimination relative to PRS contribution; many other candidates also lack PRS-only metrics, making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain.

Runners-up: PGS000078 and PGS000789 are endpoint-faithful (incident lung cancer) with very large European evaluation (n=392,539) and consistent reported full-model AUROC/C-index (~0.846/0.849) plus HR per SD (~1.16–1.17), but they include extensive smoking/environment/family-history covariates that reduce comparability to standalone PRS. PGS000740 has strong reported full-model AUROC (0.811) and substantial validation (n=167,955) but is explicitly restricted to early-onset lung cancer (<50 years), which is a phenotype mismatch for generic lung cancer. PGS004884 is incident lung cancer with HR 1.24 and C-index 0.62, but has a very small listed training sample (n=404) and only moderate discrimination evidence in the selected record.

All 12 visible candidates are direct matches to the target concept (lupus erythematosus) via either the exact EFO term (PGS001870, PGS002082) or the closely aligned systemic lupus erythematosus endpoint (most others). The best-supported direct-match choice is PGS002082 because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: “Lupus (localized and systemic)”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (361,553), and comes from a portability study with explicit multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS), which is supportive for generalizability. Main limitation: it reports only a weak PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0212) and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2, so comparative performance evidence across candidates is limited.

Runners-up: PGS001870 is the same endpoint/publication family but uses penalized regression with far fewer variants (87) and slightly lower partial-r (0.0184), making it a weaker sibling. Among disease-focused SLE scores, PGS000328 has the strongest reported discrimination signal in the list (full-model AUROC 0.83) with a clear SLE phenotype (though restricted to early-onset), but AUROC is full-model and covariates are unknown. PGS000754 (lassosum; 293,684 variants) is structurally strong and SLE-aligned but shows lower full-model AUROC (0.65) and mixed-ancestry evaluation with selected European record. PGS000196 is SLE-aligned with moderate full-model AUROC (0.79) but is a sparse P+T score (55 variants) with small validation (n=245) and unknown covariates. Overall, because most candidates lack PRS-only metrics and several have endpoint restrictions (renal disease, nephritis subtype, early-onset, or EHR packaging), the direct-match set supports a choice but not a clearly high-certainty winner.

Direct-match candidates are present for the target trait (lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia). PGS000788 is best supported among the direct lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia models because it has coherent endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), large European evaluation (n=391,338), and comparatively strong effect-size evidence (HR=1.7 per SD) alongside strong reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; additionally, PGS000788 uses inverse weights from PGS000077, making it closely tied to that prior score rather than an independently derived PRS.

Runners-up ranked by remaining direct-match support: (1) PGS000077 is the closest sibling with the same 75-variant construction and the same incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint and large EUR evaluation (n=391,338), but with weaker effect size (HR=1.45) and slightly lower full-model AUROC (0.719). (2) PGS000645 is an exact lymphoid leukemia label with PRS-comparable metrics including an OR per SD (1.358) and pseudo-R2 (0.0193), but it is extremely sparse (6 variants) and has much smaller evaluation (n=957) with modest AUROC (0.578). (3) PGS002305 maps to lymphoid leukemia (trait_efo) and reports AUROC ~0.57, but has small evaluation (n=265) and limited metadata (unknown covariates; no effect sizes). (4) PGS000874 is a strong chronic lymphocytic leukemia score (C-index 0.861; OR 3.79) but its phenotyping is explicitly restricted to individuals with a family history of hematological cancers, reducing direct-match generalizability to the broad target trait despite being within the lymphoid leukemia spectrum.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to macular degeneration/age-related macular degeneration by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS004606 is best supported overall because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS/meta-analysis context (Nat Genet 2024; IAMDGC), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~1.0M), and reports a full-model AUROC (0.71) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.73–1.78) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10). Main limitation: it does not report PRS-only AUROC/R², so the AUROC is not directly comparable as a standalone PRS metric.

Runners-up: (1) PGS004952 has very strong reported full-model AUROC (listed as 0.842, though the classification_metrics AUROC appears inconsistently encoded as 84.2) and is endpoint-specific to late AMD, but its validation sample is small (n=1,232) and it is a GWAS-hits score (52 SNPs), making robustness less clear. (2) PGS004607 is a sibling PRS-CS model from the same Nat Genet study but with weaker reported discrimination/effect size (AUROC 0.65; OR 1.48) and a GWAS ancestry mismatch (AFR GWAS, EUR eval). (3) PGS001013 is an exact-label macular degeneration model with explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.553; PGS-only R² ~0.006) and incremental AUROC reported, but it is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (813 traits) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models. (4) PGS002269 is labeled AMD but its phenotyping_reported is a retinal layer thickness biomarker endpoint (proxy/adjacent phenotype), reducing endpoint fidelity for direct disease-risk deployment despite multi-cohort context.

Direct-match candidates for melanoma are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma endpoints). PGS000813 is best supported in the visible list because it has strong endpoint alignment (familial cutaneous melanoma in non-carriers of CDKN2A mutation; still melanoma diagnosis), reports comparatively strong discrimination (full_model AUROC=0.77 with age/sex covariates) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.12), which is supportive of PRS signal strength. Key limitation: its endpoint is a restricted familial/non-CDKN2A subgroup rather than a general-population melanoma endpoint, so generalizability is uncertain; additionally, most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not PRS-only), limiting strict comparability. Runners-up were ranked by maintaining direct melanoma endpoint fidelity while favoring stronger reported discrimination/effect sizes in broadly incident invasive melanoma settings: PGS000743 (AUROC=0.74 but small validation n=1,035 and heavy traditional risk-factor covariates), then PGS002247 and PGS002246 (incident invasive melanoma with AUROC ~0.69 and R2 ~0.07), then PGS000766 (incident cutaneous melanoma with C-index=0.643 and HR=1.46).

All 6 listed candidates are nominal direct matches on concept (trait_reported and trait_efo align to multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma), but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS003450 is internally inconsistent because phenotyping_reported is "Chronic lymphocytic leukemia" despite trait_reported "Multiple myeloma", so it is deprioritized as endpoint-incoherent. Among the remaining coherent models, PGS002281 has the strongest visible validation discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.644 with CI 0.622–0.666) and a strong stratification metric (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles), with phenotype reported as multiple myeloma and only basic covariates (age, sex, geographic region), making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the provided metadata. Confidence is not High because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so the AUROC values are not strictly comparable PRS metrics per the provided domain guidance; additionally, PGS002306 shows an even higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but on a much smaller validation sample (n=290) with unknown covariates, creating meaningful competition and uncertainty. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS002306 next for highest AUROC but limited/unclear evaluation context; then the coherent PRSweb siblings (PGS000653, PGS000654, PGS000652) with similar basic covariates and moderate full-model AUROC (~0.576–0.577) and per-SD ORs ~1.32 (where available), with PGS000653 slightly favored over PGS000654 by marginally higher AUROC/R² and effect size, and PGS000652 last due to smaller training and weaker AUROC.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002726 is preferred because it is disease-focused (IMSGC training), endpoint-aligned (MS), EUR GWAS/EVAL, and shows the strongest reported discrimination signal among candidates with explicit AUROC (full_model AUROC=0.80; also reports a large risk-gradient OR top 10% vs median=15). However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC is full-model (covariates listed as Unknown) rather than explicitly PRS-only, and several strong competitors exist with different strengths: PGS000809 is also disease-focused multi-cohort with basic covariates and reports full-model AUROC=0.765 plus R²=0.069 and β=0.63; PGS002038 and PGS001831 come from a portability framework paper (penalized regression / LDpred2) with partial-r metrics only (no AUROC/R²) but structurally strong genome-wide methods; PGS004699 has very large validation size and AUROC=0.752 but is framed in an optic neuritis presentation context and still lacks PRS-only metrics. Given these comparability limitations and mixed metric types, confidence is Moderate rather than High. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction, including PheCode 411.2 and ICD10 I21 acute MI). Among the visible direct MI models, PGS005039 is best supported by (i) tight phenotype alignment (Myocardial infarction; PheCode 411.2), (ii) strong reported discrimination in the selected European validation record (C-index 0.7848, among the highest shown), and (iii) strong per-SD effect size evidence (OR 1.578, which is in the ‘strong’ range per the provided domain guidance). Runners-up are other near-identical MI PheCode 411.2 models from the same publication family with similarly high C-index and strong ORs: PGS005035 (C-index 0.7834; OR 1.541), PGS005045 (C-index 0.7839; OR 1.554), PGS005044 (C-index 0.7836; OR 1.546), and PGS005038 (C-index 0.7831; OR 1.53). Confidence is not High because many candidates are effectively a near-clone set with very small metric differences, and several other direct MI endpoints exist (e.g., UKB snpnet MI variants and ICD10 I21 acute MI models) but lack comparably strong PRS-isolating evidence (often only full-model metrics or weaker HR), making the ‘best’ choice sensitive to small, non-decisive differences in the visible metadata.

Direct-match candidates are present (2/2) and both are tightly phenotype-aligned to the target: trait_efo="Nasal Cavity Polyp" and phenotyping_reported="J33 (Nasal polyp)" for both PGS004465 and PGS004535, with matched EUR-only development/evaluation context and identical training/validation cohort context (UKB; training n=174,489; validation n=56,192). With no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported for either model (all AUC/R2 fields null; covariates unknown), the main differentiator available is the reported per-SD effect size: PGS004535 reports a stronger OR (1.600668) than PGS004465 (1.3496), which is supportive evidence of stronger PRS discrimination per the provided domain guidance. However, confidence is limited because both models come from the same publication family with largely identical metadata and missing key comparable performance metrics/covariate details, making the ranking reliant on a single effect-size field.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to nicotine dependence via trait_efo and report the same endpoint label/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder) from the same UKB portability publication with similar basic covariates and identical training/validation sample sizes, so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiator in the visible evidence is PRS-comparable performance: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697) in the selected European validation record, supporting PGS002037 as the best-supported direct match. Confidence is Moderate because both models come from a portability/framework-style paper (a known weaker archetype vs disease-focused studies) and only partial-r is available (no AUC/R2/effect sizes shown), limiting the strength of the recommendation and leaving the two candidates otherwise near-clones.

Direct-match candidates are present: multiple models explicitly target nodular goiter entities ("Benign nodular goiter" and "Nontoxic multinodular goiter"). For the target trait "nodular goiter", the closest phenotype alignment is the benign nodular goiter set (PGS005261/5262/5263), whereas the UKB portability scores (PGS001814/PGS002022) are aligned to the narrower "nontoxic multinodular goiter" endpoint and come from a portability framework paper. Among the benign nodular goiter siblings, PGS005262 is best supported by the visible performance evidence (highest reported full-model AUROC 0.5933 within that endpoint family) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), a positive structural signal versus the P+T alternative (PGS005261, 110 variants). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: the two case-control contrast endpoints (PGS005273/PGS005274) still include benign nodular goiter explicitly but are not pure nodular-goiter endpoints; they have higher AUROC but are discounted because they are thyroid-carcinoma-vs-benign classification rather than generic nodular goiter risk. Next is the other benign nodular goiter PRSCS sibling (PGS005263) with slightly lower AUROC, then the P+T benign nodular goiter model (PGS005261). Confidence is moderate (not high) because (i) the benign nodular goiter models report only full-model AUROC with covariates listed as Unknown (so PRS-only comparability is unclear), and (ii) the UKB multinodular-goiter models provide PRS-comparable partial-r but are from a portability framework and target a somewhat different endpoint, creating unresolved tradeoffs.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported. The best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS005235 because it has strong endpoint fidelity despite the broader label (“Adiposity”) by using an explicit obesity phecode endpoint (phenotyping_reported: “Obesity (phecode: 278.1)”), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with high variant count (709,828), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97), which domain guidance treats as strong discrimination evidence when AUC/R2 are absent. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004447 (E66 obesity, LDpred2, very high variant count, moderate OR≈1.36 but covariates unknown), then PGS005154 and PGS005145 (both obesity endpoints in an East Asian-focused evaluation with only beta effect sizes and no comparable PRS-only metrics), then PGS004517 (same study family as PGS004447 but weaker OR≈1.23). Confidence is Moderate (not High) because most candidates lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2, several have unknown covariates, and two large UKB framework/portability candidates (PGS001298/PGS001825/PGS002033) provide some PRS-only/partial-r evidence but are penalized by domain guidance as framework-style scores and/or weaker endpoint fidelity (e.g., time-to-event or broad administrative phenotype bundle), leaving residual uncertainty in cross-study comparability.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo includes osteoporosis; phenotyping_reported is osteoporosis or a closely aligned ICD10 subtype such as M81). The best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS001273 because it has clear endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis) and, uniquely among the pool, reports explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.5685; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00688) plus incremental AUROC, enabling interpretation of PRS contribution (and showing the high full-model AUROC is largely covariate-driven). However, confidence is limited because PGS001273 (and PGS001274) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused scores; meanwhile several newer disease-focused candidates report only effect sizes (OR/beta) without PRS-only AUC/R2, making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001274 is similarly well-documented with slightly higher PRS-only metrics but has a time-to-event subtype endpoint (osteoporosis without pathological fracture), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for generic osteoporosis; PGS002768 has clean phenotype alignment and a moderate per-SD OR (1.31, with CI) but lacks PRS-only AUC/R2; among the 2024 Commun Biol cluster, PGS004565 and PGS004560 show the strongest reported per-SD ORs (~1.33) within that family but have unknown covariates and limited comparable metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is the generic disease endpoint (“Otosclerosis”), aligning better with a generic otosclerosis target than PGS001255’s time-to-event endpoint (“TTE otosclerosis”), which domain guidance flags as a potential weakness when the target is generic disease risk. However, the evidence is limited and conflicted: PGS002046 lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R² (only partial-r=0.0182 is provided), while PGS001255 reports PRS-only AUROC (0.6319) and PRS-only R² (0.01341) plus full-model AUROC (0.6532) with basic covariates, but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance warns often generalizes poorly. With only these two candidates and no external-validation-focused disease study family available, the best choice remains uncertain, lowering confidence and yielding a DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL outcome.

Direct-match candidates are present, including multiple models explicitly mapped to the target EFO term (ovarian neoplasm) with phenotyping_reported = "Malignant neoplasm of ovary" (PGS000544–PGS000564 family), plus many near-synonymous ovarian cancer / ovarian carcinoma models. For direct-match to the target trait label, the ovarian-neoplasm EFO/phenotype-aligned cluster is the most endpoint-faithful.

Within that endpoint-faithful cluster, PGS000549 is best supported by the visible comparable performance evidence: it has the highest reported full-model AUROC among the ovarian-neoplasm models shown (0.567, EUR eval) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.263, 95% CI 1.15–1.387), with consistent EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry. Runners-up are selected from the same ovarian-neoplasm endpoint family with very similar design but slightly weaker AUROC/OR evidence: PGS000550 (AUROC 0.568 but similar; OR 1.286), PGS000551 (AUROC 0.558; OR 1.234), PGS000560 (AUROC 0.552; OR 1.233), and PGS000564 (AUROC 0.556; OR 1.215).

Main limitation: across these candidates, the reported AUROC values are full-model metrics with covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided here; several models are near-clones with small metric differences, so the best-vs-runner-up separation is modest, lowering confidence. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 11 visible candidates are direct matches to the target concept (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma, with one clinically dominant subtype model (PGS002264: pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) also plausibly aligned. PGS000083 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), large European evaluation (n=391,491), and comparatively strong effect-size evidence (HR=1.49 per SD; C-index ~0.742) within a coherent multi-cohort cancer-focused evaluation context. However, confidence is not High because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with substantial covariate adjustment (including family history and smoking/BMI), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, limiting comparability across models. Runners-up: PGS000794 is essentially the same 22-variant score family with similar full-model discrimination/effect size but uses inverse weights (making it less straightforward as a primary pick despite similar evidence). PGS000663 and PGS000725 are same 22-variant genome-wide-significant constructions with acceptable endpoint alignment but smaller/less informative validation contexts (e.g., n=956 for PGS000663) and/or weaker metric package. PGS002264 reports a high AUROC (0.83) but is heavily discounted because it is a subtype endpoint (PDAC) and appears to be a risk-prediction package integrating diabetes status and other clinical risk covariates, making the AUROC non-comparable as PRS evidence.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease), but several have endpoint mismatches (progression/cognitive decline/dementia) or covariate-heavy full-model reporting that limits PRS-only comparability. PGS000903 is best supported because it targets Parkinson’s disease status (phenotyping_reported: “Parkinson’s disease”), comes from a major disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication family (Lancet Neurol 2021; same family as PGS000902), uses a more polygenic construction (C+T; 1,805 variants), and is the only candidate here with an explicit PRS-comparable metric (reported R²=0.054) plus a strong stratification effect (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25). Main limitation: the AUROC shown (0.692) is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only) and covariates include age/sex/PCs, so cross-model metric comparability remains imperfect; several other direct PD models exist with different designs/metrics, preventing high confidence.

Runners-up: PGS000902 is the closest sibling from the same Lancet Neurol meta-analysis with identical endpoint/covariates but weaker visible discrimination evidence (lower full-model AUROC 0.651 and no R²/OR shown). PGS003763 has strong endpoint fidelity for incident PD and a large cohort with a clear HR (1.72 high vs low tertile), but it is incident-only and lacks PRS-only metrics. PGS000123 is a clean PD-status endpoint with a significant association and per-score beta reported, but lacks standard PRS discrimination metrics and is smaller/older. PGS001353 is a direct PD endpoint with time-to-event style HR evidence in an Asian cohort (useful when ancestry matches), but it is ancestry-specific and uses only 6 variants, limiting general support for a generic PD target.

All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches for the target concept (peripheral vascular disease), but they split into (i) two UKB portability-framework scores labeled “Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified” (PGS001843, PGS002055) and (ii) two disease-focused peripheral artery disease (PAD) scores (PGS005158, PGS005217). Given domain guidance prioritizing endpoint fidelity and disease-focused study archetype over portability-framework scores, PGS005217 is best supported: it targets incident PAD (a clinically central manifestation within peripheral vascular disease), is from a PAD-focused multi-cohort study (many contributing cohorts listed), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with large variant count (1,296,292), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.66, 95% CI 1.61–1.71) plus a C-index/full-model metric (0.731) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), reducing concern about covariate-driven inflation. Main limitation: the target is broader than PAD and the reported discrimination is not explicitly PRS-only (no PGS-only AUC/R2), so direct comparability across candidates remains imperfect.

Runners-up: among the two portability-framework PVD-‘unspecified’ models, PGS002055 is preferred over PGS001843 because it has a stronger PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0175 vs 0.0151) and a more polygenic method/structure (LDpred2 with 599,514 variants vs penalized regression with 242 variants), though both remain penalized by the portability-framework context and weak partial-r magnitude.
